general_rules.description: Internal team members (same domain @strategyco.com) receive casual greetings (first name only), short closings (initials or 'Cheers'), and direct action-oriented language without formality.

External clients and senior stakeholders receive formal greetings ('Dear [First Name]' or 'Dear [Title] [Last Name]'), full signature block closings ('Best regards, James Conseil'), and structured, detailed communication.
Emails to internal team include specific action items numbered or bulleted, with clear ownership and deadlines (e.g., 'by Wednesday', 'by Thursday').
Client-facing emails (external contacts) are longer, more narrative-driven, include executive summaries, and emphasise value and strategic alignment.
Travel and logistics requests to Emma Phillips are brief, casual, and use 'Hi Emma' or 'Emma,' with minimal formality despite being administrative.
Emails to peers on the same engagement (Ben, Anika, David) use collaborative language ('Let's', 'We'll') and provide constructive feedback with specific slide/section references.
Formal external emails include full title and company affiliation in the signature block; internal emails omit the signature block entirely.
Feedback to team members is specific and actionable, referencing slide numbers, data gaps, or deliverable quality, rather than generic praise.
Strategic updates to leadership (Richard Hayes) are concise, use bullet points, include financial metrics (revenue, utilisation, margins), and end with 'Cheers, J.' without full signature.

Emails to external contacts in non-English-speaking regions (Klaus, Takeshi, Isabelle) are written in English but maintain heightened formality and cultural sensitivity language ('I would be honoured', 'I am mindful of').
